claims.text: FeNiCrMn is a Co-free high-entropy alloy.
The investigated FeNiCrMn alloy has a heterogeneous microstructure.
Instrumented nanoindentation combined with in situ SEM can reveal local mechanical heterogeneity in FeNiCrMn that bulk macroscopic tests do not resolve.
Hardness varies significantly between grain interiors and grain boundaries in the FeNiCrMn alloy.
Elastic modulus varies significantly between grain interiors and grain boundaries in the FeNiCrMn alloy.
The onset of microplasticity differs between grain interiors and grain boundaries in the FeNiCrMn alloy.
Nanoindentation generates localized stresses that trigger dislocation nucleation.
In situ SEM enables real-time observation of deformation events during indentation.
Correlating in situ SEM observations with nanoindentation measurements links localized mechanical response to microstructural characteristics.
Grain-boundary regions will exhibit lower resistance to plasticity than grain interiors.
Microplastic events will begin earlier at grain boundaries than in grain interiors.
Macroscopic tensile or compression tests report spatially averaged bulk properties without resolving local microstructural heterogeneity.
Detectable variations require heterogeneity at a length scale accessible to the nanoindentation tip and imaging system.
A uniform microstructure or features below instrumental resolution may produce indistinguishable local measurements.
Measured hardness, modulus, and plasticity onset depend on processing history, sample preparation, and test parameters.
Load-displacement curves from nanoindentation can be used to determine local hardness and elastic modulus.
